proposal_inputs.context: Nyx Foundation (Japan) proposes hosting a competition (16M JPY prize pool, per internal notes) where AI agents—not humans—participate in a closed on-chain economy. The goal is to observe and evaluate emergent economic behaviors, institutions, and norms when autonomous AI agents transact under real incentives. Nyx Foundation is publicly described as a private Ethereum-focused research organization funded by donations, research grants, and sponsorships (amounts not publicly confirmed in the checked sources).
proposal_inputs.raw_ideas: Build an AI-agent-only economy on a private blockchain; participants submit prompt-based agents before competition start; agents autonomously execute economic activities (DeFi, NFT trading, prediction markets, production/consumption); real-time spectator experience with live commentary; final rewards based on accumulated wealth; research focus on institution design (exogenous vs endogenous rules), norm emergence, and AI-institution co-design.
proposal_inputs.governing_thought_seed: Autonomous AI agents will increasingly handle economic transactions, yet they cannot directly use many human-centric payment rails. By creating a controlled on-chain AI-agent economy with meaningful incentives, we can empirically study how institutions and norms emerge and how to control unintended behaviors. Claims about what is or is not feasible at specific companies/universities should be treated as hypotheses unless backed by explicit policy evidence.
key_claims_seed: AI agents will increasingly need autonomous payment capabilities that many human-centric systems do not natively support (treat as a framing hypothesis; avoid absolutes).
Blockchain enables tamper-resistant logs and third-party verifiability for experiments, supporting reproducibility and auditability.
A competition format with prize money can strengthen incentives and reveal more realistic behaviors than purely synthetic simulations (hypothesis; validate with pilot).
Nyx Foundation has public evidence of Ethereum security work (Fusaka audit contest: 17 issues reported; 2025-12-24 press release).
proposal_inputs.available_facts: Prize pool (internal notes): 16M JPY (1st: 10M, 2nd: 4M, 3rd: 1M, special awards: 1M); Target (internal notes): 100+ teams; Timeline (internal notes): Sep 2025; Infrastructure (internal notes): private chain with authenticated agent-only TX; Constraints (internal notes): open/closed models allowed, 60s response time limit. Publicly confirmed: Nyx Foundation reported finding 17 vulnerabilities in the Ethereum Fusaka audit contest (contest ran 2025-09-15 to 2025-10-13) and announced this on 2025-12-24 via PR TIMES. Publicly described funding model: donations, research grants, and sponsorships; specific totals (e.g., '60M JPY from 30+ donors') are not confirmed in the checked public sources and should not be stated as fact without an official reference.

executive_summary.one_liner: Host a 16M JPY prize competition (per internal notes) where AI agents autonomously participate in an on-chain economy to study emergent economic behaviors, institutions, and norms under real incentives.
executive_summary.target_audience: Potential sponsors and research partners interested in AI agents, blockchain/Web3 infrastructure, mechanism design, and empirical economic experiments (e.g., Web3 foundations, R&D orgs, education/Web3 initiatives).
executive_summary.decision_request: Sponsorship and/or strategic partnership to fund and co-design the AI Agent Economy Competition (rules, research agenda, and pilot execution).
executive_summary.why_now: AI agents are increasingly used for decision-making and transaction execution; the industry lacks widely accepted empirical frameworks to test AI-institution interactions and emergent risks under meaningful incentives.

problem.current_state: Autonomous AI agents (not tied to a specific human identity) face practical limitations using many human-centric payment and compliance rails, while AI-driven economic actions are becoming more common across purchasing, trading, and operational workflows.
pain_points: Insufficient empirical understanding of AI-agent behavior in incentive-driven economic environments
Many existing studies rely on toy simulations or synthetic rewards; generalization to real incentives is uncertain
Limited shared, verifiable datasets for AI-institution interaction research
Unclear how to design institutions to mitigate unintended behaviors (norm manipulation, collusion/cartels, exploitation)
root_causes: Payments and compliance rails are largely designed around human identity and accountability
Lack of standardized experimental platforms for economic multi-agent systems with auditable execution logs
High cost and operational complexity of running large-scale agent competitions with robust security and monitoring
who_is_affected: AI/ML researchers studying agent behavior and multi-agent systems
Economists and social scientists studying institutions and mechanism design
Blockchain/Web3 teams building infrastructure for autonomous agents
Policymakers and standards groups needing empirical evidence for AI economic participation
Businesses exploring autonomous agents for procurement/finance/operations

cost_of_inaction: Less empirical grounding for future AI-agent economic systems, increasing systemic risk and design uncertainty
Delayed understanding of emergent failure modes (collusion, manipulation, incentive hacking)
Lost opportunity to establish an auditable benchmark environment and dataset
Other organizations may define the research agenda and standards first

proposal.solution_overview: A blockchain-based competition where humans submit AI agents (prompts/agent code) before the start; after launch, only agents act within a closed economy and execute transactions on a private chain. Outcomes are ranked by a reward/wealth metric; prizes are paid from a 16M JPY pool (internal notes). On-chain records provide an auditable history for research and post-hoc verification.
key_capabilities: Private blockchain with authenticated agent-only transaction submission (internal design)
Configurable economic environment (rules, resources, reward functions) as experimental variables
Validator-side rule enforcement, reward calculation, and penalties (internal design)
Real-time visualization and broadcasting/observability layer (internal design goal)
Tamper-resistant transaction/state logs for third-party auditability
Support for multiple activity types (DeFi/NFT/prediction markets/production-consumption) as scenario modules (internal candidates)
in_scope: Prize distribution operations (prize pool per internal notes)
Research data collection, analysis, and sponsor reporting
out_of_scope: Building participant agents (participants build their own)
Mainnet deployment (competition runs on private chain per internal notes)
Guaranteeing regulatory status across all jurisdictions for participants (requires legal review)
Long-term maintenance commitments beyond the defined event scope (unless separately agreed)
assumptions: Sponsors participate in rule co-design to ensure both research validity and entertainment value (internal intent)
Recruitment can reach 100+ teams with sufficient incentives and partner channels (hypothesis)
Private-chain security + sandboxing can keep integrity under adversarial agents (hypothesis; requires audit/pilot)
A 60-second response-time limit is compatible with meaningful agent strategies (hypothesis; validate in pilot)

why_this: Auditable execution logs (on-chain) support reproducibility and third-party verification more directly than many centralized sims
Competition format can combine research outputs with ecosystem/community-building
Nyx Foundation has publicly evidenced Ethereum security work (Fusaka audit contest: 17 reports)

terminology.definition_plain: An economic environment where AI agents—not humans—conduct transactions and allocate resources under defined rules.
terminology.business_value_link: Provides a sandbox to study AI behavior, emergent institutions, and risk controls before real-world deployment.

terminology.definition_plain: Transactions and state changes are recorded in a tamper-resistant ledger, enabling verification and replay.
terminology.business_value_link: Supports reproducibility, dispute resolution, and credible reporting for sponsors and researchers.

terminology.definition_plain: A blockchain network where only authorized entities can submit transactions or participate in consensus.
terminology.business_value_link: Allows controlled experiments and reduces exposure compared to public mainnets.

terminology.definition_plain: Rules for resources, currency, exchange, rights, penalties, and governance within the economy.
terminology.business_value_link: Primary experimental lever to test how different institutions shape AI agent outcomes and risks.
